provenance: tests/matched.py fixture run tag v4 (code after the five review fixes; masks = the library's own release rules), k = 256, eps = 0.25, N = 10,000, seeds 0 and 1
notes: Final release table: the top-level keys 's<seed>:<group>:<variant>'. Released fields with a frozen tolerance: ic_log_gain_max, ic_E_trace, ic_strain_sq, ic_spin_sq. slope_fraction and heldout_ic are an in-sample budget and an out-of-sample score, released (mask relmotion_fitsplit) as measured quantities; their rows compare them with values built from the analytic derivative (slope part tr(K Gc K^T); oracle score with the true differential) and are characterisation, not release criteria. pre_identity_gate holds the largest log gain released by the free-intercept gates alone (mask strain_finite_ic), i.e. before the 'beat the no-deformation score by 0.3' gate (final mask gain_ic). Gate exception (Rules.flow, identity_exact_min = 0.95): the 0.3 margin over the no-deformation score is waived where that score is itself >= 0.95 (essentially undeformed, near noise-free neighbourhoods, e.g. a rigid rotation, which scores 0.97 and cannot clear a 0.3 margin; in this fixture the rotation control's gains are released through it, all within tolerance); no released value of the lens grid used it. Noisy-identity control (controls:identity_noise0.6): after the gate the largest gain is released on 38 (seed 0) and 43 (seed 1) of 10,000 points (0.4%), of which 37 and 42 exceed the 0.1 tolerance: coverage is negligible and the accuracy of the few released points is poor. The statement 'at most 2-10% false releases under scatter' refers to the deforming-map variants (smooth, weak-axis, rank-8, near-singular, fold), not to this control.
gates_null_means: a gate value of null is a disabled cap (no upper limit), e.g. cond_max_strain: flow mode uses the centred-design cap cond_centred_max instead of the uncentred one
